speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The other baker. High Street. Gilbert's ticket says not the first baker. One and forty shillings.

speaker: (the baker)
text: One and forty it is. I have had it on the leaf since before Lady Day.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Count it with me. Twenty. Thirty. Forty. And the shilling. The belt had fifty-eight when I came out.

speaker: (the baker)
text: Forty-one. I will rule the page from corner to corner.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Rule it off clean, and say nothing at the door in Henley Street.

speaker: (the baker)
text: A paid leaf does not walk. My tongue stays behind my teeth.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Seventeen shillings are left in the belt. Sheep Street will not be paid out of seventeen.

speaker: (the shoemaker)
text: Four and forty shillings and sixpence. Shoes and the mending, and it has stood.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Seventeen is on the board. It is short. The canvas was sixty, sewn, and meant for Anne. I am taking two and forty out of it.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Two and forty out. Eighteen stays in the cloth. Seventeen and forty-two is fifty-nine.

speaker: (the shoemaker)
text: I am naming four and forty and six. I am not naming a gift.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Pay yourself four and forty and six. Fourteen and six remains. That is the whittawer, by the bridge. Skins.

speaker: (the shoemaker)
text: Four and forty. The sixpence. Sound silver. The page is ruled. Henley Street will not hear of it from this shop.

speaker: (the whittawer)
text: Fourteen and six, and the skins were for your father's bench. I have the penny. I rule the leaf.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Say nothing at his door. He likes his own time with a book.

speaker: (the whittawer)
text: A ruled page is a silent page. I do not carry news with a hide.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Three pages ruled. Five pounds. Forty-two of them out of the Lady Day cloth. Eighteen left in it.

speaker: (the shoemaker)
text: Your seam is open. That is your business, and not my bill.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I will sew it before the house sees it. No names go home with me.

speaker: (the baker)
text: The High Street is done. I have my nothing, and I am keeping it.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Fifty-eight from the belt, forty-two from the canvas. One hundred shillings. I will not say the total where my father can hear it.

speaker: (the whittawer)
text: I did not hear a father. I heard a page. It is ruled.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Then the pages are done. The man who is owed nothing has not had his say, and I am not giving him a name to carry.

speaker: (the baker)
text: Cross the street as you must. My leaf is crossed already.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I cross with the cloth still open and the eighteen in it. No name comes with me.
